human_tolerance.notes: Described as readily adapting to human habitation, seen on wires and telephone posts near towns and in almost all public spaces of large cities; it can be an agricultural pest on grain.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: 'No fixed breeding season is seen in most of their range, and provided with plentiful food and habitat, birds breed almost continuously', so the phase covers the whole year.

vocalizations.description: A deep, soft 'oo-ah-oo', repeated in a rising and falling series from a wire, post or tree; also used in the steep-climb and semicircular-glide breeding display.

taxonomy.note: Rank and accepted name from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy.

external.note: GBIF usage key from the GBIF Backbone match for the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id and Wikidata Q-id from Wikidata.

conservation.note: The article's taxobox gives the IUCN status as LC.

range.note: The Spanish article's distribution section says only 'Vive comunmente en Sudamerica, habiendo aparecido pequenas colonias en Trinidad y Tobago y las Antillas Neerlandesas', which does not enumerate countries. The country list here is a conservative selection of the South American range the article describes and is not an exhaustive transcription.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Eared doves feed mainly on seed and grain taken from the ground', walking to forage, and 'Its flight is high, fast, and direct'; the record declares those two gaits. Swimming and climbing are not described.

traits.nest_type.note: 'It builds a small stick nest several meters up in a tree' - a thin stick platform, which the schema calls a Platform.

traits.perching.note: Described as 'being seen on wires and telephone posts near towns' and nesting in trees.

traits.mass_kg.note: 'The eared dove is 24 cm long with a long, wedge-shaped tail, and weighs normally about 112 g.'

traits.length_m.note: 'The eared dove is 24 cm long with a long, wedge-shaped tail.'

traits.wingspan_m.note: Neither Wikipedia article states a wingspan. Derived as roughly 1.4x body length (0.24 m), the usual span-to-length ratio for a medium pigeon or dove, giving about 0.34 m. This is an approximation, not a sourced figure.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No open-licensed source gives a typical or maximum lifespan for Zenaida auriculata: the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles, Wikidata and GBIF carry none, and the field-guide and Animal Diversity Web pages were avoided under the licence policy. 5.0 years is a documented judgement placeholder, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Diet-Seed 100 (BirdFuncDat row, Diet-Certainty A). The article is explicit: 'Eared doves feed mainly on seed and grain taken from the ground', with 'animal foods, such as caterpillars, insect pupae, aphids and snails' only augmenting the diet, so the record keeps a single seed share.

traits.social.note: 'This is a gregarious bird when not feeding or nesting'; group_size is a judgement for a flock of doves.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Nocturnal 0; the bird feeds on the ground and perches on wires by day.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flushes from the ground to a wire or tree when approached, the escape the shared ground-forager program encodes.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from the described habit of feeding in almost all public spaces of large cities and on telephone posts near towns.

habitat.use.note: ForStrat-ground 20, ForStrat-understory 20, ForStrat-midhigh 40, ForStrat-canopy 20; the mid-high and canopy shares are mapped to arboreal, giving 0.2 ground against 0.8 arboreal.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts on wires, posts and in trees between feeding bouts.

habitat.resources.note: The seed weight follows the EltonTraits diet share of 100; perch and nest_platform follow the described perching and nest sites.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and road_mortality from 'it readily adapts to human habitation, being seen on wires and telephone posts near towns ... in almost all public spaces of large urban areas' and from its pest status in grain fields; light_max is a judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'No fixed breeding season is seen in most of their range, and provided with plentiful food and habitat, birds breed almost continuously' - the bird is present and breeding year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: 'No fixed breeding season is seen in most of their range, and provided with plentiful food and habitat, birds breed almost continuously', so the phase spans 01-01 to 12-31 rather than a fixed window.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'It builds a small stick nest several meters up in a tree and lays two white eggs. These hatch in 12-14 days with another 9 days to fledging.' duration_days 21 is the midpoint 13 + 9 (rounded), and scale is a judgement for a recently fledged bird.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The species' call is a deep soft oo-ah-oo.'

look.note: 'Adult males have mainly olive-brown upperpart plumage, with black spots on the wings. The head has a grey crown, black line behind the eye, and the blue-black on the lower ear coverts ... The underparts are vinous, and the tail is tipped with cinnamon. The bill is black and the legs dark red.' Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program: seed-based foraging with a walking gait, a daytime rest window, and flee and calm distances for a bird that habitually feeds in the open.
